question: I just received Canadian permanent-resident status. Is the issue date on that immigration document automatically my Canadian income-tax residency start date? What else matters?
generated_answer:
What is the issue date on your immigration document? The issue date is the date on which your immigration document was issued. This date is important because it determines when you became a Canadian permanent resident. The issue date is also used to determine your Canadian income-tax residency start date. The Canadian income-tax residency start date is the date on which you became a Canadian permanent resident. This date is used to determine when you are required to file a Canadian income-tax return. The Canadian income-tax residency start date is also used to determine when you are eligible to claim certain Canadian income-tax credits and deductions. In addition to the issue date, there are other factors that can affect your Canadian income-tax residency start date. These factors include:

- The date on which you became a Canadian citizen

- The date on which you became a Canadian permanent resident

- The date on which you became a Canadian resident for tax purposes

- The date on which you became a Canadian resident for immigration purposes

- The date on which you became a Canadian resident for social security purposes

- The date on which you became a Canadian resident for health care purposes

- The date on which you became a Canadian resident for other purposes

If you have any questions about your Canadian income-tax residency start date, you should contact the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) or a tax professional.
